media.transcript: Can you separate a real painting from a computer generated one? Let's find out. This is Two Truths and AI. Number one. Number two. Number three. Number three. This one was tough. So let's think it through. AI generated images can sometimes get the proportions wrong. Could that be why this boy's head looks a little too large for his body? Or was that the artist's choice? We also know that image generators can struggle with creating realistic text. They can sometimes mush together letters, mix different font styles, or even invent characters. The cat painting has a signature on it that looks authentic. But while text can be a useful clue, it's not a guarantee that something is or isn't AI. Now, let's zoom in on the horse painting. We can see lots of detail in the brush strokes, which makes me think that it's legit. But notice how both the man's legs are behind the horse? Is that an AI tool making a mistake? A great way to tell if an image is AI generated is by doing a reverse image search. There are several reverse image search tools out there. But today I'm going to use one called TinEye. What we'll do is save or screenshot the image, head to TinEye.com, upload it, and carefully look through the matches. Okay, now for the actual answer. The boy with the book? That's a real painting. It was titled J. Ellis Bonham and was painted in 1825 by William Bunnell. And from my search, I learned that it's currently held at the Art Institute of Chicago. The cat painting? Yeah, that's also real. This piece is called Winter Cat on a Cushion and was painted in 1909. As for the horse painting, TinEye could not find a horse painting. single matching results. Now if you do a reverse image search and you don't get any results, it doesn't automatically mean that it is AI generated. But in this case it's pretty telling. For a genuine piece of art you would expect it to be paired with basic details like the title, the artist, the year it was made. And if you can't seem to find any of that information be skeptical or at the very least file it away as unconfirmed. But I can tell you for a fact that this one is AI because we pulled it from Midjourney's Explorer page. Did you get it right this week? Let us know in the comments and stay tuned for the next episode of Two Truths in AI.
